channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Brussels signals unwillingness to be Burnham’s sounding board on EU options
item.description: The British prime minister wants to gauge what's possible with the bloc before laying out options to voters back home. EU diplomats say it may not be so straightforward.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU asylum agency floats idea of foreign ‘processing centres’ to handle asylum claims
item.description: Innovative solutions is a catch all phrase that describes return hubs in Rwanda and Italy's controversial deal with Albania. Now it also applies to "process centres" for asylum seeker hopefuls.

item.description: First public remarks since revelations over extramarital affairs forced co-founder to resign

item.title: [Financial Times] US tech stocks slide ahead of Nvidia results
item.description: Nasdaq 100 down 1.4% after volatile run of trading

item.title: [Politico Europe] Le Pen defends retirement reform plan as opponents mock her economic credibility
item.description: The far-right leader says her plan to lower the retirement age would be offset by savings and employer-funded pension schemes.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Jusqu’où peut aller David Lisnard ?
item.description: Tutoyant désormais la barre des 10% dans les dernières intentions de vote pour la présidentielle, le maire de Cannes prend de vitesse ses concurrents. En quoi cette percée rebat-elle les cartes à droite et au centre ? Le fondateur de Nouvelle Energie peut-il être freiné dans son ascension par l’élection pour la présidence pour l’AMF, […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Ukraine destroys section of Crimea bridge in fierce exchange
item.description: Part of key Russian road crossing collapses and parallel rail bridge damaged while Moscow hits infrastructure in Ukrainian capital

item.title: [DW] Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
item.description: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

item.title: [EU Observer] France dethrones Sweden as EU gender equality leader — but overall progress is slowing
item.description: Europe still has a significant gender gap. It's in employment, in who takes care of children, in places of power. It's stronger in places like Cyprus and Bulgaria, while Spain and Denmark prioritised its gender politics. But full gender equality is still a distant goal, as Europe still lags behind pre-pandemic levels of parity.

item.title: [DW] Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
item.description: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU countries push to shut Russia out of Venice Biennale
item.description: Poland leads the charge against Russia taking part at Venice Architecture Biennale

item.description: Daughter and son-in-law come under scrutiny as board launches probe over company’s links to Megaspeed

item.description: The EU climate commissioner urged ministers not to be distracted by a plethora of demands

item.description: Central bank governor says attending ‘unfair’ proceedings would endanger the ‘institution’s unique status and independence’

item.title: [Euractiv] Europe has recognised the nutritional gap in cancer care. Now action must follow. [Promoted Content]
item.description: Up to seven in ten people with cancer face malnutrition, yet only one in five is assessed for it. The European Parliament has called for change. Now health systems must deliver.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU freezes €62.5m of Slovakia’s recovery funds over plans linked to ousted environment minister
item.description: Internal government warnings, downgraded wind plans and controversial zoning tweaks by ousted environment minister Taraba’s team now emerge at the heart of the Commission’s decision, exposing how months of behind-the-scenes manoeuvring may have sabotaged Slovakia’s own green transition money.

item.description: Countries were asked to weigh in on testing, cybersecurity, and international cooperation

item.description: Grzegorz Braun faces up to five years in prison for allegedly detaining a doctor who had performed an abortion.

item.description: The two countries also want to allow temporary national bans

item.description: The Ukrainian president gave details of a weeks-long operation aimed at crippling a crucial Russian transport route that also has symbolic meaning for Vladimir Putin.

item.description: NGOs say Rwanda's human rights record means deportation hub plans fail EU and international law requirements.

item.description: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission again rebukes Temu over failure to stop illegal product sales, exposing Chinese giant to another hefty fine
item.description: Temu failed to take sufficient action to stop illegal or unsafe products being put on sale, the EU Commission has found preliminarily. It comes as part of a probe into the company's compliance with the Digital Services Act. The Chinese shopping website has disputed the latest findings.

item.description: Several member states want more detail on Brazil’s antimicrobial compliance system

item.description: Regulator says it has significant concerns about the use of personal data that is being collected by AI agents.

item.description: Eurozone debt will rise from 89.6% of economic output this year to 91.3% in 2028.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Germany poised to nominate Brunnermeier as ECB chief economist
item.description: The chief economist’s position is one of three top jobs that European governments are aiming to fill by year-end.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Czech MEP Niedermayer slams Babiš opposition to new EU budget revenue: ‘It’s short-sighted’
item.description: From missed IT revolutions to costly nuclear bets, EU Parliament's economic policy vice-chair Luděk Niedermayer sketches a stark choice for European capitals: keep blaming Brussels for their woes, clinging to national budgets, or allow the EU to levy its own targeted taxes on negative externalities to better compete with the US and China.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What do France’s centre-right candidates want for Europe?
item.description: In the race for the French presidential election, there are already four names on the centre-right: Gabriel Attal, Bruno Retailleau, David Lisnard and Édouard Philippe. For now, they haven't reached an agreement to join forces and put forward a single candidate.

item.title: [EU Observer] Vacancy: Senior Editor, EUobserver

item.description: Email, internal probes and other documents throw new light on the career and leadership of chief executive Christian Sewing

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘Katastrophe’: inside the chaos at Germany’s biggest bank
item.description: Millions of leaked documents cast light on Christian Sewing’s leadership of the scandal-hit lender

item.title: [EU Observer] Only Stockholm, Helsinki and Copenhagen meet EU air pollution rules, as stricter enforcement looms
item.description: Apart from Copenhagen, Stockholm and Helsinki, no other major European city currently meets the revised EU limits for nitrogen dioxide and particulate matter - exposure to which caused a combined 216,000 excess deaths in 2023 alone.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Forever chemicals’ lobbyists met EU Commission 37 times in push to escape ban ahead of key decision
item.description: As the European Chemicals Agency finalises its conclusions on so-called 'forever chemicals', a new report reveals regular contact between senior European Commission officials and industry lobbyists.

item.description: President’s allies trade blame over losing grip on new media landscape after crushing midterm defeat

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress to make her debut at first earnings
item.description: Successor to founder Jensen Huang will have to ease investors’ anxiety about AI chipmaker’s future

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [DW] Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: [DW] Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Emperor’s New Clothes’: Burnham breaks 10-year taboo on Brexit
item.description: Boris Johnson's 'oven ready' Brexit deal never tasted very good. That's part of the 'obvious truth' about Brexit, according to UK PM Andy Burnham.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, drones likely hit arch (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,726)
item.description: Ukrainian drones pound the Crimean Bridge and Russian tanks stall in fog near Dobropillia. In the meantime, commanders on both sides are gambling lives and prestige on offensives that keep collapsing under precision strikes.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s mandate on Russia-Ukraine peace talks takes shape, as Putin escalates war
item.description: While Europe crafts its role in the Ukraine peace talks, Vladimir Putin’s renewed offensive raises the cost of every EU decision.

item.title: [EU Observer] Five EU countries tout Rwanda deportation partnership, but no formal deal as key details remain secret
item.description: Rwanda is set to host a so-called EU return hub. No formal deal has been announced as technical details still need to be sorted out in negotiations. The hope is to start deporting people next year.

item.title: [EU Observer] More EU sanctions on Russian propagandists and hackers, as thousands of fake accounts target voters
item.description: The EU agreed on Monday (16 November) to sanction 30 people and two organisations over Russian cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns targeting Europe, as researchers uncovered thousands of fake accounts used to target election campaigns.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Georgia has reached final stage of autocratic consolidation,’ warns former deputy foreign minister
item.description: Georgia’s fall from EU frontrunner to near-total state capture is not just a regional tragedy but a case study in how Russia exploits European complacency to pull an entire country back into its orbit, explains former minister.

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
